**You will be trusted to take ownership of complex projects and to make your voice heard. You will be supported to perform at your best, grow your skills through hands-on experience across Novo’s value chain and relevant learning offerings, and develop others by mentoring less experienced colleagues.

Salary: For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from 742,600.00 to 1,091,600.00 DKK, corresponding to the level of the position.

The placement within the salary range will be assessed during the recruitment process based on the candidate’s skills, competencies, knowledge, and relevant experience.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area, and relevant market benchmarks.

Learn more about our Reward Philosophy here.

**Start now

**Your impact begins today. If you are ready to lead complex projects that create value across Novo, apply for the Senior Project Manager role by 8th November 2026. Applications are reviewed on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality of opportunity for all our job applicants.

jobs.occupation: Projektkoordinator
jobs.description:
Do you want to keep projects on track through effective coordination and high-quality documentation? Can you combine attention to detail with an overview of tasks, processes and deadlines? And do you have experience supporting project managers? Then join COWI as our new Project Coordinator!

Create the solutions that will enable a better tomorrow

We are looking for a Project Coordinator to join COWI and support our customers’ construction and operational projects. You will help ensure that work follows the applicable project model and act as a sparring partner to project managers and provide coordination, administrative support and document management across assignments.

Your key responsibilities will be:

• Take responsibility for project documentation, including preparing documents, reviewing and revising documentation, and ensuring it is archived in accordance with agreed rules.

• Maintain project registers to support progress and results, and share lessons learned about document management across the organisation.

• Act as a sparring partner to the project manager, assist with financial follow-up, and on your own coordinate, carry out and complete ad hoc tasks to relieve the project manager

• Plan, facilitate and report on workshops, and organise meetings, prepare agendas and write minutes.

• Develop process diagrams and guidance for project participants, and create, design and administer project workspaces.

• Train and support users of project-related tools and prepare status reports and project website content.

Your official COWI office location will be either Lyngby, Vejle or Aarhus. However, your primary workplace will be at Energinet in Erritsø, but Ballerup could also be an option, with some travel to Erritsø. You will report to Head of Discipline, Ioana Nicoleta Tuglui, who is based at COWI's headquarter in Lyngby.

Your skills. Our team. Together we design the future.

You enjoy collaborating with colleagues and external partners and bring a proactive and positive approach to your work. As the project’s administrative anchor, you are approachable, service-minded and flexible, while standing firm on quality requirements for processes and deliverables. You work in a structured way, maintaining an overview without losing sight of the details. You are curious about new tasks and also comfortable with routine work forming a substantial part of your day.

On top of that, you will have:

• Proficiency in Danish and English, both written and spoken.

• Experience with document management and an understanding of its importance to project quality and handover.

• Experience from a similar role in project coordination or project administration.

• An aptitude for IT, the ability to work across administrative systems, a good understanding of Microsoft Office and familiarity with SAP

• The ability to organise and see tasks through from start to finish, working with both internal colleagues and external partners.

A place to work and so much more

At COWI, we work together with our customers to shape a sustainable and liveable world. We do it by applying our knowledge and curiosity – and sometimes even our courage – to create the solutions the world needs today to enable a better tomorrow. We support our customers’ transition towards increased sustainability. We strive to lead by example by embedding environmental management, social responsibility and good governance into our business practices and the options we provide to our customers.

We value differences and development and cultivate an environment of belonging and having fun. Because that is what brings out the best in you, at work and at home.

With offices primarily located in the Nordic region, the UK, North America and India, we are currently more than 7,500 people who bring their expertise in engineering, architecture, energy and environment into play.

Get to know us even better at our website, www.cowi.com, where you can learn more about our projects, our strategy, what we want to achieve and what life is like at COWI.

Before you apply

All you need to include in your application is your CV – no photo or application letter. At an interview, you can tell us everything we need to know about why you’re interested in joining COWI. As for the photo, we prefer to form our first impression in person rather than from a picture.

Diversity is fundamental to COWI, inclusion is key

We are committed to creating a respectful and fair work environment where all employees have a sense of belonging and equitable opportunities to thrive and grow. We ensure that our leaders are role models for inclusive leadership by cultivating a culture where diverse perspectives and thoughts are seen as strengths. And we take diversity and inclusion into account in all relevant decisions and processes and when setting teams and fora. We do it because it is part of our values and because it is simply the right thing to do.

jobs.occupation: Revenue Manager
jobs.description:
atNorth is a leading Nordic data center company providing cost-effective, scalable high-density colocation and built-to-suit services to industry-leading organizations across Iceland, Sweden, Finland, and Denmark.

With sustainability at our core, our data centers run on renewable energy and are designed according to circular economy principles. Through innovative design, power efficiency, and intelligent operations, we deliver reliable, secure, and high-performance infrastructure.

Headquartered in Reykjavik, Iceland, atNorth operates eight data centers across the Nordics, with additional sites under development in Finland, Denmark, Sweden and Norway.

We combine world-class technology with a people-first culture built on collaboration, ownership, and trust, empowering our teams to grow, take responsibility, and make a real impact.

By joining our international team, you will help shape the future of sustainable digital infrastructure.

Revenue Manager at atNorthAs a Revenue Manager, you will act as a trusted commercial partner to Sales and business leaders, helping ensure that growth is both profitable and sustainable. By combining financial insight, commercial understanding and market awareness, you will support pricing decisions, evaluate commercial opportunities and help improve the processes that drive long-term customer and company value.

This is a highly collaborative role for someone who enjoys balancing commercial ambition with financial discipline and is comfortable constructively challenge in order to support better decision-making.

**Key responsibilities:

**

• Analyse customer opportunities, pricing proposals, commercial terms and contract structures to support revenue growth and profitability.

• Partner closely with Sales and business stakeholders, providing independent commercial and financial perspectives on deals and opportunities.

• Assess how pricing, capacity, delivery timing, customer commitments and cost to serve affect deal value and long-term profitability.

• Develop revenue forecasts and scenarios based on contracts, pipeline, capacity plans and customer growth assumptions.

• Monitor revenue and profitability performance and identify risks, trends and opportunities across customers, services and markets.

• Support commercial decision-making through business cases, analysis and recommendations.

• Help establish and continuously improve commercial governance, pricing processes and decision frameworks.

• Identify opportunities to increase customer value through pricing, utilisation, contract renewals, additional services and expansion opportunities.

• Provide clear analysis and insights for leadership discussions and commercial reviews.

**Your profile:

**

• A Bachelor's or Master's degree in Finance, Economics, Business or a related field.

• Several years of experience in revenue management, commercial finance, pricing, business partnering or a similar commercially focused analytical role, ideally within the data centre industry or other asset-intensive businesses operating long-term contractual and capacity-based commercial models.

• Strong understanding of pricing, profitability, commercial decision-making and customer value creation.

• Experience partnering with commercial and sales teams while maintaining an independent and objective perspective on pricing, profitability and commercial decision-making.

• The confidence to challenge assumptions and influence decisions while building strong relationships across the business.

• Strong analytical capabilities and the ability to translate data into practical recommendations.

• Excellent communication skills and confidence working with senior stakeholders across different functions.

• Professional proficiency in English.

**Experience That Would Be Particularly Relevant

**

• Experience building or improving commercial processes, governance frameworks or decision-making structures.

• Exposure to BI tools, analytics platforms, AI-enabled solutions or other technologies supporting commercial performance and decision-making.

**Who You Are

**You are commercially minded, analytical and collaborative. You understand that successful growth requires both strong sales execution and sound commercial decision-making.

You are comfortable asking difficult questions and challenging assumptions when needed, but you do so in a constructive way that helps teams move forward together. You enjoy working across functions, building relationships and bringing structure to complex situations.

Just as importantly, you're a team player who values collaboration over hierarchy. At atNorth, we believe great ideas can come from anywhere, and we look for people who are supportive, humble and eager to help others succeed.

**About The AtNorth Culture

**We believe that sustainable success starts with the wellbeing of our people. For us, an open, transparent, and inclusive culture is more than a priority, it is the core of how we lead and innovate.

We don’t just talk about culture; we nurture it. Through regular one-to-one engagements and monthly wellbeing surveys, we listen carefully to our teams, ensuring that every voice is heard and every opportunity for improvement is embraced.

We recognize that innovation and collaboration thrive where people feel truly connected, which is why we come together each week to share ideas, strengthen relationships, and nurture a sense of belonging, sometimes over a simple breakfast and good conversation.

At atNorth, we are building a community where you can do your best work and shape a sustainable future together.

jobs.occupation: PhD in Physical AI for Adaptive Robot Manipulation
jobs.employer_name: Technical Sciences - Institut for Electro- og Comp
jobs.description:
PhD in Physical AI for Adaptive Robot Manipulation
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Electrical and Computer Engineering programme. The position is available from 01 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
PhD in Physical AI for Adaptive Robot Manipulation

Research area and project description
Applications are invited for a fully funded three-year PhD position at the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, Aarhus University. The position is part of STORM (Soft Tactile Memory for Safe Physical-AI Correction of Robotic Foundation Models), a new project funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark (DFF). The candidate will join the Adaptive & Agentic AI (A3) Lab, headed by Dr. Behzad Bozorgtabar (main supervisor), and will work closely with Professor Ahmad Rafsanjani and the SDU Soft Robotics group, who are developing the soft tactile skin.

Research vision
How can a robot foundation model use physical feedback to correct an action during execution? Models such as vision-language-action (VLA) and world-action models let robots follow natural-language instructions, but they act on what they see rather than on what they feel. When a grasp begins to slip or a fragile object deforms, the camera view often looks fine until the damage is done. STORM gives robotic foundation models a sense of touch, so that a robot can notice when a manipulation is going wrong and correct itself safely while it acts.

PhD project
The candidate will develop the machine-learning core of STORM. The work spans three connected scientific questions, leaving room for the candidate to shape the specific algorithmic directions: (1) How can contact representations be learned from advanced tactile interfaces, including a soft-fluidic tactile skin developed at SDU? (2) How can predictive models forecast how contact states should evolve over short horizons under a policy's intended actions? (3) How can the mismatch between expected and felt contact drive parameter-efficient adaptation of pre-trained foundation policies while guaranteeing safety? Methods will be evaluated on public benchmark and real-world robotic setup, focusing on dexterous manipulation of fragile and unseen objects as well as safe human-robot interaction.

Environment
The project sits at the intersection of machine learning, Physical AI, robot foundation models (e.g., VLA and World-Action models), world models, tactile sensing, and adaptation algorithms—areas in which the A3 Lab publishes regularly at top-tier venues such as NeurIPS, ICLR, CVPR, and CoRL. The PhD includes a possible planned research stay at KTH Royal Institute of Technology in Stockholm, and close collaboration with the SDU team.

Qualifications and specific competences
This is a highly selective position; applicants are expected to meet the requirements below.

Education: A master’s degree (120 ECTS or equivalent) in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, Robotics, Electrical/Computer Engineering, or a related quantitative field, completed or nearing completion before the start date.

Technical Skills: Advanced proficiency in Python and PyTorch, with hands-on experience training, fine-tuning, or adapting modern deep architecture such as Transformers, state-space/sequence models, and diffusion or flow-matching models.

Core Knowledge: A strong foundation in machine learning, deep learning, or computer vision, combined with a strong motivation to work on Physical AI, multimodal tactile sensing, world models, and online adaptation, etc.

Relevant Research Experience (one or more of the following is highly advantageous):
 
• Robot & Policy Learning: Imitation learning, behavior cloning, offline/model-based RL, or policy learning for manipulation (e.g., diffusion policies, Vision-Language-Action models, or World-Action models), as well as familiarity with manipulation benchmarks (e.g., LIBERO, CALVIN, or ManiSkill).
• World Models & Sequential Representation Learning: Self-supervised learning on temporal or multimodal sensor streams, action-conditioned video/dynamics prediction, latent world models, or uncertainty estimation.
• Model Adaptation & Post-Training: Test-time adaptation (TTA), continual/online learning, parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT/LoRA), or safe/constrained policy updates.
Hands-on Robotics: Prior experience with physical robot platforms, grippers, tactile/force sensors, and ROS 2 is an advantage, but not strictly required for candidates with an exceptional machine learning background. However, a strong willingness to work with physical hardware and run real-robot experiments is required.

Track Record: Evidence of strong research potential—such as a strong master’s thesis, open-source research code, or publications/submissions at leading ML, vision, or robotics venues (e.g., NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, CoRL, RSS, ICRA)—is a strong advantage.

Attributes: A mindset for scientific rigor, reproducibility, and open-source contribution, the ability to collaborate across algorithmic AI and physical hardware teams, and excellent written and spoken English.

Application Requirements (How to Apply)
Please ensure your application includes the following documents:
• Statement of Interest (1 page): Detailing your background in machine learning, computer vision or robotics, any work experience relevant to the position, and your motivation for joining the A3 Lab and the project.
• Curriculum Vitae: Including a publication list (if applicable) and a technical project page, with links to code repositories or videos of experiments where available.
• Academic Records: Transcripts and diplomas (Bachelor’s and Master’s).Project Description Requirement: The candidate is required to use the project description from the PhD announcement.

Place of employment and place of work
The place of employment is Aarhus University, and the place of work is Adaptive & Agentic AI (A3) Lab, Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE), Faculty of Technical

jobs.occupation: New paradigm to disentangle hydrothermal stresses and assess regional agricultural vulnerability to drought-heatwave events
jobs.description:
Applicants are invited for a PhD fellowship/scholarship at Graduate School of Technical Sciences, Aarhus University, Denmark, within the Agroecology programme. The position is available from 15 March 2027 or later. You can submit your application via the link under 'how to apply'.

Title
New paradigm to disentangle hydrothermal stresses and assess regional agricultural vulnerability to drought-heatwave events

Research area and project description
The Department of Agroecology at Aarhus University, Denmark, invites applications for a three-year PhD position in remote sensing and knowledge-guided machine learning to assess agricultural vulnerability to drought and heatwaves. The expected starting date is 15 March 2027. The position is supported by the Sino-Danish Center for Education and Research (SDC) and involves collaboration with Chinese Academy of Sciences, including a research stay of 12 months.

Food security, climate change and biodiversity loss represent three major environmental sustainability challenges. The Center for Landscape Research in Sustainable Agricultural Futures (Land-CRAFT), established in June 2022, with expertise in biogeochemistry, agronomy and climate-impact research. This PhD project aims to develop a knowledge-guided machine-learning framework that combines remote sensing, field observations and process-based models to disentangle interacting stresses and assess agricultural vulnerability at regional scales. The research will distinguish the effects of soil water limitation, vapour pressure deficit, and temperature on crop productivity. The resulting knowledge and methods will support early warning, precision irrigation and agricultural climate-risk assessment.

The PhD student will work on three interconnected research tasks:
1. Develop an integrated observation framework for crop drought and heat responses. Combine thermal infrared, multispectral and hyperspectral remote sensing with soil moisture measurements, meteorological observations and field data to characterise crop responses across contrasting environmental conditions.
2. Disentangle the individual and interacting effects of water and heat stress. Quantify how soil-water availability, atmospheric demand and temperature influence crop functioning and productivity, and identify the conditions under which their interactions intensify crop stress.
3. Assess regional agricultural vulnerability to compound drought–heatwave events.
Scale the identified stress-response relationships from field observations to regional assessments, identifying vulnerability patterns, critical thresholds and hotspots.

SDC is a partnership between all eight Danish universities and the University of Chinese Academy of Sciences (UCAS). It brings together Danish and Chinese research and education environments through collaborative research, joint supervision and international mobility. Participation offers the PhD student opportunities to gain research experience in both countries and build an international scientific network.

More about SDC

The student will be employed at Aarhus University, with Sheng Wang as the main supervisor with Kiril Manevski, Suxia Liu and Yongqiang Zhang as co-supervisors. During the research stay in Beijing, the student will collaborate with the hydrology and land-surface modelling group at the Institute of Geographic Sciences and Natural Resources Research, CAS. The student will contribute to SDC’s MSc educational activities. The SDC framework offers the option of pursuing a double PhD degree from Aarhus University and UCAS, subject to an institutional agreement and fulfilment of both universities’ requirements. SDC PhD framework.

For further information, please reach out swan@agro.au.dk.

Demonstrated oral and written communication skills in English are required. The applicant should be enthusiastic about working in an international and interdisciplinary academic environment. Applications from women and people from underrepresented groups are strongly encouraged. Further, we will prefer candidates with some of the following qualifications:

 * Advanced Programming & Big Data: Strong programming skills (preferably in Python) and experience handling large-scale, multi-source remote sensing datasets and cloud-computing platforms.
 * Rich experience in satellite remote sensing for crop yield prediction and stress analysis. Good scientific and technical writing skills.
 * Strong skills in programming (preferably in Python), large-scale remote sensing data processing, radiative transfer modelling and deep learning. Direct experience or strong background in deep learning or knowledge-guided machine learning.
 * An ability to communicate effectively in English, and will contribute to dissemination, teaching and reporting research outcome in high-impact scientific journals.

jobs.occupation: Student Assistant - Data & Analytics (BluePool and Data Governance)
jobs.description:
Do you want to help shape the future of Europe’s energy system and contribute to a fully carbon‑neutral, sustainable power grid? Are you a data engineer who is curious, open‑minded, and initiative-taking — someone who enjoys working in an explorative and collaborative environment? Do you want to collaborate with engineers, application developers, and data scientists to unlock insights from the vast amounts of data behind our services?

We are looking for a Student Assistant to support our Data & Analytics department. This is an excellent opportunity for a student who wants practical experience working with data platforms, governance processes, documentation, and operational support activities in an international and highly technical environment.

**Nordic RCC – supporting security of supply and the green energy transition

**Nordic Regional Coordination Centre (RCC) provides critical services and insights to support the national Transmission System Operators (TSOs) in Finland, Norway, Sweden and Denmark — to ensure the efficient operation and use of the Nordic power system and high security of power supply at any time.

Based in Copenhagen, Nordic RCC is one of six RCCs in Europe, equally owned by the Nordic region's four electricity TSOs: Fingrid, Statnett, Svenska Kraftnät, and Energinet.

As European power systems integrate and evolve to meet climate goals, Nordic RCC provides regional coordination, integrated services, regional insights and recommendations to the Nordic TSOs and their control centres, to support cross-border operational security 24/7.

Join Nordic RCC, a fast-developing company determined to make a significant impact in the energy sector and to provide for a secure and efficient transition to the green, sustainable energy system.

Right now, we are looking for a Student Assistant to join our Data & Analytics Department.

**What You Will Be Working On

**The Data and Analytics team consists of 10 employees and consultants and plays a central role in enabling data-driven decision-making across Nordic RCC. The team develops and maintains data pipelines, analytics products, BI solutions, platform services, and information services that support operational, strategic, and regulatory needs.

As Student Assistant, you will support various initiatives across the department, with a primary focus on NRCC's analytics platform ‘BluePool’, and data governance activities.

**Examples Of Tasks May Include

**BluePool Support

• Assisting with user onboarding and access administration

• Maintaining onboarding guides and user documentation

• Supporting training sessions and workshops

• Gathering and tracking user feedback

• Assisting with testing of new BluePool functionality

Data Governance

• Supporting data governance processes and documentation

• Maintaining data catalogues and metadata documentation

• Assisting with data classification and governance activities

• Supporting compliance and process-related initiatives

General Department Support

• Coordinating meetings and workshops

• Maintaining team documentation and knowledge bases

• Preparing presentations and communication materials

• Supporting project coordination and follow-up activities

• Assisting with ad hoc analytical and administrative tasks

**Who We Are Looking For

**You are currently enrolled in a relevant university programme, for example within data science, computer science, engineering, information management, business analytics, economics, mathematics, or a similar field.

You do not need extensive professional experience. What matters most is that you are curious, structured, and comfortable taking ownership of practical tasks — from organizing documentation and following up on details to supporting colleagues with day-to-day needs.

**We Are Looking For Someone Who

**

• Is detail-oriented and follows tasks through carefully

• Enjoys turning information into clear documentation, guides, or overviews that others can use

• Communicates clearly in writing and verbally

• Can work independently while also asking for input when needed

• Has an interest in data, analytics, and digital platforms

• Is comfortable using Microsoft Office tools

It is an advantage, but not a requirement, if you have experience with one or more relevant tools or concepts, such as Python, SQL, Power BI, enterprise architecture, data governance, or technical documentation.

**What We Offer

**

• A flexible student position that can be adapted to your studies

• Exposure to large-scale data and analytics initiatives within the energy sector

• Experience working in an international environment with Nordic stakeholders

• Insight into data governance, analytics platforms, and digital transformation

• Opportunities to build practical skills that are highly relevant for a future career in data and analytics

• A friendly and collaborative team with experienced data scientists, data engineers, and analytics specialists

**Application & Security Clearance

**Please apply online in English no later than 5 November 2026. Interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis.

To ensure a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly request that you do not include photographs in your CVs or application materials.

A cover letter is not required, but we kindly ask you to include a few sentences in your CV explaining why you are interested in the position. Applications are only accepted through our online recruitment system.

Note that as part of the recruitment process, the candidate must undergo a satisfactory background check. The position is also conditioned upon a national security clearance. Both will be facilitated by Nordic RCC. You can read more on security clearance here. Please also note that the process includes that any spouse, registered partner, cohabitant, steady partner, co-resident, child over 18 living at home and parent with the same address as the candidate must also consent to be examined.  Nordic RCC is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

jobs.occupation: Associate Director, Global Drug Safety & Pharmacovigilance Physician
jobs.description:
At Genmab, we are dedicated to building extra[not]ordinary® futures, together, by developing antibody products and groundbreaking, knock-your-socks-off KYSO antibody medicines® that change lives and the future of cancer treatment and serious diseases. We strive to create, champion and maintain a global workplace where individuals’ unique contributions are valued and drive innovative solutions to meet the needs of our patients, care partners, families and employees.

Our people are compassionate, candid, and purposeful, and our business is innovative and rooted in science. We believe that being proudly authentic and determined to be our best is essential to fulfilling our purpose. Yes, our work is incredibly serious and impactful, but we have big ambitions, bring a ton of care to pursuing them, and have a lot of fun while doing so.

Does this inspire you and feel like a fit? Then we would love to have you join us!

**The Role

**This role provides medical oversight of product safety, including adverse event review, ongoing safety surveillance, and management of emerging safety issues. Responsibilities include safety input to clinical and regulatory deliverables, aggregate reporting, safety committee oversight, cross-functional collaboration, and ensuring regulatory compliance and inspection readiness.

**Responsibilities

**

• Perform medical review of Adverse Events reports for Genmab products.

• Perform ongoing surveillance of safety data from Genmab clinical trials.

• Ensure handling of safety issues.

• Perform medical review and provide input to e.g., Trial Protocols and amendments, Trial Reports, Trial plans, eCRFs/CRFs, TMFs, Investigator’s Brochures, Subject Informed Consent, Development Safety Update Reports, Integrated Safety Summaries, scientific articles, and medical reviews.

• Prepare aggregated reports and safety summaries in accordance with regulatory requirements.

• Responsible for the establishment and management of external Data Monitoring Committees (DMCs)

• Chair and manage Genmab Safety Committees

• Conduct training of Genmab employees, CROs and Investigators

• Member of Clinical Management Teams (CMTs), Compound Development Teams (CDT) and Compound Strategy Teams (CST) and contribute to multidisciplinary project groups and provide input to clinical development programs.

• Interact with safety and clinical CROs and perform sponsor oversight activities.

• Collaborate with external experts and partners.

• Contribute to multidisciplinary project groups.

• Ensure compliance with regulatory guidelines and internal procedures in order to be prepared for audits and inspections.

• Participate in audit and inspection activities as relevant

**Requirements

**

• Medical degree (MD or equivalent) with relevant clinical experience; oncology or hematology experience preferred.

• 8+ years of experience in pharmacovigilance, drug safety, or clinical development within the pharmaceutical/biotechnology industry.

• Demonstrated experience in adverse event medical review, safety surveillance, signal evaluation, benefit–risk assessment, and aggregate safety reporting.

• Experience providing medical safety input to clinical trials and regulatory deliverables, including protocols, Investigator’s Brochures, informed consent documents, DSURs, clinical study reports, and integrated safety summaries.

• Strong knowledge of global pharmacovigilance and clinical development requirements, with experience supporting Safety Committees/DMCs, regulatory submissions, audits, and inspections.

• Strong medical judgment, leadership, and communication skills, with demonstrated ability to collaborate across functions, CROs, external partners, and regulatory stakeholders.

• Experience executing processes/projects in own area (e.g. guidance documents as per intl. regulations & reporting requirements; preparation of post-marketing spontaneous and clinical trial safety assessments; regulatory submissions; safety case processing; PV data systems; safety data base systems and the report generation)

• Experience working with FDA/EMA/PMDA/ICH requirements, good clinical practices, and pharmaceutical clinical development

• Experience guiding team members around complex issues

For US based candidates, the proposed salary band for this position is as follows:

$200,000.00---$300,000.00

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Also, certain positions are eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as discretionary bonuses and long-term incentives.

When You Join Genmab, You’re Joining a Culture That Supports Your Physical, Financial, Social, And Emotional Wellness. Within The First Year, Regular Full-time U.S. Employees Are Eligible For

• 401(k) Plan: 100% match on the first 6% of contributions

• Health Benefits: Two medical plan options (including HDHP with HSA), dental, and vision insurance

• Voluntary Plans: Critical illness, accident, and hospital indemnity insurance

• Time Off: Paid vacation, sick leave, holidays, and 12 weeks of discretionary paid parental leave

• Support Resources: Access to child and adult backup care, family support programs, financial wellness tools, and emotional well-being support

• Additional Perks: Commuter benefits, tuition reimbursement, and a Lifestyle Spending Account for wellness and personal expenses

Further details on eligibility for compensation and benefits based on role will be provided during the recruitment process

**About Genmab

**Genmab is an international biotechnology company with a core purpose to improve the lives of patients through innovative and differentiated antibody therapeutics. For 25 years, its hard-working, innovative and collaborative team has invented next-generation antibody technology platforms and harnessed translational, quantitative and data sciences, resulting in a proprietary pipeline including bispecific T-cell engagers, antibody-drug conjugates, next-generation immune checkpoint modulators and effector function-enhanced antibodies. By 2030, Genmab’s vision is to transform the lives of people with cancer and other serious diseases with Knock-Your-Socks-Off (KYSO®) antibody medicines.

Established in 1999, Genmab is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark with international presence across North America, Europe and Asia Pacific. For more information, please visit Genmab.com and follow us on LinkedIn and X.

Genmab is committed to protecting your personal data and privacy. Please see our privacy policy for handling your data in connection with your application on our website Job Applicant Privacy Notice (genmab.com).

Please note that if you are applying for a position in the Netherlands, Genmab’s policy for all permanently budgeted hires in NL is initially to offer a fixed-term employment contract for a year, if the employee performs well and if the business conditions do not change, renewal for an indefinite term may be considered after the fixed-term employment contract.

jobs.occupation: Scientific programmer and data analyst in Environmental Science
jobs.description:
Would you like to apply your programming and data analysis skills to research and environmental advisory work addressing air pollution and climate change? We are looking for a scientific programmer and data analyst to help develop, modernize and operate atmospheric models and analyze complex environmental datasets. You will join the Section for Atmospheric Emissions and Modelling at the Department of Environmental Science, Aarhus University, working closely with researchers on both scientific projects and research-based advice to public authorities. 

The Section for Atmospheric Emissions and Modelling conducts research and provides research-based advice on atmospheric processes, emission inventories, air pollution and climate modeling, integrated impact assessment for health, nature and climate, and land-use and remote-sensing research. You will play an important role in advancing this work through the development and improvement of scientific models and the analysis and interpretation of complex environmental data.

This is a permanent position based in Roskilde, Denmark, with an expected starting date of February 1, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Expected start date and duration of employment

This is a permanent position starting 1 Feb 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.

Job description
You will participate in research and advisory projects, the latter mainly for the Danish Ministry of Environment. Both research and advisory projects aim to understand atmospheric processes, helping ministries and environmental agencies regulate air quality and protect our environment. You will work in a dynamic and multidisciplinary team of researchers. 

Together with researchers, your main task will be to restructure, improve and modernize existing air quality models and forecast systems as well as to contribute to the development of new integrated air pollution models. A key part of your role will be to help modernize our scientific codebase by introducing and applying good software development practices, making our models and workflows easier to maintain, document, test and reproduce. Your tasks will also include developing and automating workflows for computationally demanding model simulations, including parallel computing, and the processing of large datasets, as well as developing and maintaining applications and scripts in Linux and Windows environments.

You will have the opportunity to collaborate with various research groups and shape the Section’s data science strategy. In addition, you will take part in department-wide initiatives such as workshops, presentations and events related to data science, and contribute to reports and scientific publications.

Your profile
We welcome applications from candidates who meet most, though not necessarily all, of the following qualifications:

 * An MSc or PhD in computer science, software engineering, physics, applied mathematics or a related field
 * Advanced programming skills in languages such as Python, R, Fortran, C/C++ or similar, including experience with scientific computing, data analysis and visualization libraries
 * Experience with implementing and applying modern software development practices for scientific computing, including code organization, version control, documentation, testing, maintainability and reproducibility, as well as experience with parallel computing
 * Experience in handling and analyzing large datasets

We are looking for a curious, proactive and motivated colleague who is keen to develop new technical skills and acquire knowledge of atmospheric and air pollution science. Experience with the development and application of air quality models would be welcome, but is not required.

You should enjoy working both independently and collaboratively, sharing knowledge and providing technical guidance to colleagues. Good communication skills and excellent written and spoken English are important. Danish language skills are an advantage, but not a requirement.

Additional experience in any of the following areas would be an advantage, but is not required:
 * GIS and geospatial data
 * Development and integration of APIs and web-based applications
 * Working with and modernizing legacy scientific software, including Delphi or similar technologies
 * Machine learning and AI methods

About the Department 
The Department of Environmental Science is an interdisciplinary department within the Faculty of Technical Sciences at Aarhus University. Our research covers a wide range of fields, including physics, chemistry, microbiology, social sciences, geography, and environmental economics. The department conducts research and provides research-based advice to ministries and public authorities. Our work addresses major societal challenges such as pollution control, land and water management, climate change, biodiversity protection, and ecosystem services.

We have a highly collaborative work environment, where all employees contribute to securing the research and advisory projects that fund the majority of the department’s activities. We value equality, diversity, and a strong work-life balance.

The Research Group

The selected candidate will join the Atmospheric Modelling Group within the Section for Atmospheric Emissions and Modelling. The group focuses on air pollution processes and climate interactions. It develops, tests, and applies models across spatial scales, from global to local, and examines the environmental, health, and socioeconomic impacts of air pollution and climate change. Close collaboration with other sections within the department is essential, particularly in areas such as atmospheric measurements, environmental economics, and geography.

In the group, we specialize in 
 * Atmospheric physics and chemistry, including numerical methods and computer science
 * Air pollution modeling at global, regional (Northern Hemisphere, Europe, Denmark) and local scales (urban areas, point sources)
 * Numerical weather prediction models at different spatial scales
 * Integrated assessment modeling (impact on health, environment, and climate)
 * Environmental noise modeling
 * Climate modeling and its links to air pollution and health
 * Decision-support for policy makers on emissions, air quality, and health impacts

Work location 

The place of work will be at Aarhus University, Frederiksborgvej 399, 4000 Roskilde, Denmark. The city of Roskilde (www.roskilde.dk) is located approx. 30 km from Copenhagen. The area provides immediate access to a wealth of cultural and recreational pursuits. 

International candidates may find information concerning living and working in Denmark at www.workindenmark.dk. AU International Center offers a full range of services to make your transition to Denmark as smooth as possible (http://www.au.dk/en/internationalcentre/ias/), and the department will assist foreign candidates with finding a suitable place to live.

Contact information

Further information may be obtained from Professor Peter Langen, Head of the Section for Atmospheric Emissions and Modelling, at plangen@envs.au.dk or +45 2061 8369.

Deadline
Applications must be received no later than 3 Dec 2026.

Formalities and salary range
Salary and terms as agreed between either the Danish Ministry of Taxation and the Confederation of Professional Unions, where you will be employed as an academic staff member at basic salary grades 4–8, or subject to section 15 of the collective agreement for IT employees (PROSA) in the service of the state and LC/CO10-S (the Confederation of Teachers’ Unions/the Danish Confederation of Public Employees of 2010) collective agreement.

Aarhus University’s ambition is to be an attractive and inspiring workplace for all and to foster a culture in which each individual has opportunities to thrive, achieve and develop. We view equality and diversity as assets, and we welcome all applicants.

The application must be submitted via Aarhus University’s recruitment system, which can be accessed under the job advertisement on Aarhus University's website.

PhD scholarship in Experimental Clearance Flow Research - DTU Construct
jobs.description:
The PhD candidate will, as part of a collaboration project between a private enterprise and DTU Construct, carry out experimental clearance flow research with ammonia and other sustainable marine fuels. 

Pressure and temperature conditions, resembling those in a marine engine booster pump, are created in an in-house designed clearance flow test rig. Measured clearance flow data will be used to develop and validate accurate flow models. The test rig will be further modified to enable testing and evaluation of different sealing solutions.

Responsibilities and qualifications

The PhD candidate will be responsible for continuing our development of a high-pressure ammonia flow rig, conduct test campaigns with different ammonia pump components and develop both theoretical and experimental foundation for developing ammonia compatible sealing techniques.

The candidate should have significant experience with:

• Safe handling of ammonia and other liquified gases in test setups.
• Design and wiring electronic data acquisition and control systems using PC Schematics.
• LabView programming.
• Mechanical design and FEM analysis using Solid Works.
• Data processing of large experimental sets of dynamic flow and pressure data using statistical methods in Matlab.
• CMM (Coordinate Measurement Machine) measurement and preferably have experience with Calypso Software.
• Data processing large complex geometric data sets from CMM measurements for 3-dimensional analysis of tested pump components.
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment

The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

We offer

DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. Salary and appointment terms

The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information

Further information may be obtained from Anders Ivarsson, aniv@dtu.dk.

You can read more about Department of Civil and Mechanical Engineering at www.construct.dtu.dk. 

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure

Your complete online application must be submitted no later than 19 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• Curriculum vitae

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

DTU Civil and Mechanical Engineering develops and utilises science and technical knowledge for the benefit of society and the sustainable development. DTU – For the benefit of society since 1829
DTU is one of Europe's leading elite technical universities. Through research and education at an international top level, we create solutions to the major societal challenges of our time and help secure Europe's global leadership in sustainable technological development. Since Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU almost 200 years ago, our mission has remained the same: We develop and create value through the natural and technical sciences for the benefit of society.
