jobs.occupation: Declaration of interest regarding PhD project: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy
jobs.description:
Declaration of interest regarding PhD project:

The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy, with background in one or more of the following areas: philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, phenomenology.We are looking for a person with a relevant degree (M.A., MSc. etc.) in philosophy or a related field. Starting date is September 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is fully funded, full-time, for three years. The PhD degree will be awarded by the Faculty of Health Sciences.

 

Research environment

The PhD student will be based in the research group of Applied and Interdisciplinary Phenomenology in the Department of Psychology, SDU, at the Odense campus. The research group develops, disseminates, and applies methods to support cutting-edge research into subjectivity and the nature of human experience. Current group members have backgrounds in philosophy, psychology, anthropology, neuroscience, environmental studies, and pain research.

The group directly supports the professional development of its members, most of whom are postdocs or PhD students. In addition to receiving support from the project team, the PhD student will be supported by the broader group to develop their research, presentation, and teaching skills, as well as other academic skills, including those required for organizing academic activities such as workshops and conferences and for successful grant-writing. The PhD student will therefore be provided with the requisite knowledge and skills for pursuing an academic career in Europe or abroad.

The PhD student will also be provided with a work computer and a dedicated workspace at the Department of Psychology.

 

Project description

The PhD student will be part of the project, Understanding Experiences of Mood Disturbances in Depression (DEPMOOD), led by Anthony Vincent Fernandez. The project is funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark and runs for four years, starting September 1st, 2026. The PhD student will join the project for the final three years, collaborating with the PI, a psychology postdoc, and several external partners in Europe and the US, including philosophers, clinical psychologists, and psychiatrists.

The aim of the project is to establish a taxonomy of the variety of mood disturbances experienced by people diagnosed with depression, providing more precise characterizations of symptoms than those currently offered by concepts such as “depressed mood” or “anhedonia”. The project combines philosophical and qualitative methods, and includes in-depth interviews with people diagnosed with depression. The PhD student will not be expected to carry out interviews, as these will be conducted by the postdoc and external project partners. The PhD student’s primary role will be to help analyze the interview data using a combination of qualitative and philosophical methods. Their PhD thesis will therefore be a theoretical contribution, but will build upon the project’s empirical dataset.

In addition to producing a thesis, the PhD student will be required to take a variety of short PhD courses, carry out an international research stay, and fulfil light teaching duties.

The PhD student will be provided with DKK 10,000 per year for travel. Additional funds may be available.

 

Qualifications

Before the start date of September 1st, 2027, the applicant should have a master’s degree in philosophy or a related field and total course credits equivalent to 300 ECTS. Typically, this is a total of at least five years of education combined between bachelor’s and master’s degrees, with 60 ECTS obtained for every full year of study.

The candidate should have a background in philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, and/or phenomenology. Familiarity with qualitative research methods (especially analysis methods) is an advantage, but by no means required.

The candidate should be proficient in English. Proficiency in Danish or another Scandinavian language may be an advantage, but is not required.

For further information about the project, please contact:Anthony Vincent Fernandez

Department of Psychology

University of Southern Denmark (SDU)

E-mail: afernandez@health.sdu.dk

Please note that while we are happy to provide answers to questions about the position and application process, direct feedback on application materials cannot be provided.

Applications must include (in English, or with a certified English translation):

 

• 
A letter stating the interest, motivation and qualifications for the project (max. 2 pages) - upload under “Application form”.

• 
Detailed CV, including personal contact information as well as any publications or presentations

• 
Certified copy of diploma and transcripts (Master’s degree in a relevant field). If the applicant is in the process of completing their master’s degree, they should provide transcripts along with a letter from their supervisor confirming expected completion of their degree before September 1st, 2027.

• 
Writing sample of maximum 10,000 words (e.g., publication, conference paper, selection from a master’s thesis). If the sample exceeds this length, please indicate which section should be read.

• 
A document listing 2-3 references, with contact information and a brief note about your relation to the reference. Note that reference letters will only be requested for candidates invited to interview. 

At this stage, no project proposal is required. Candidates invited to interview will be asked to prepare a brief project plan.

Please do not use generative AI in the formulation of any application materials. The purpose of these materials is to gain a clear sense of you and your abilities.

Shortlisting and interviews may be used in the assessment process. 

For purposes of evaluation and assessment, application materials may be shared with external members of the project team at Aarhus University and Amsterdam University Medical Center.

Further information about the PhD-study can be found at the homepage of the University.

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format. We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluated

 

Closing date January 15th, 2027 

We expect to conduct interviews within two months of the application closing date.Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students. 

The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order)

 

Salary and Working Conditions at SDU

PhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement.Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. The base salary (excluding 18.07% pension contribution) is DKK 374,912.98   per year.

The Faculty of Health Sciences at the University of Southern Denmark is one of Denmark’s leading faculties of health sciences. With nine departments, internationally top‑class research, and a broad range of health‑related study programmes, we contribute to developing the knowledge, treatments, and healthcare system of the future.

As an employee at the faculty, you become part of an ambitious and interdisciplinary environment characterised by high academic standards, strong collaborations, and excellent opportunities for professional development. The faculty has activities in Odense, Esbjerg, and Copenhagen. In Esbjerg and Copenhagen, strong academic communities provide the framework for research and education, while our modern faculty building in Odense brings research, education, and administration together under one roof and is directly connected to Odense University Hospital.The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

The Research Unit of General Practice at the Institute of Public Health, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a 2-year full time Assistant Professor position in Global Health. The position starts on April 1, 2027, and will terminate at the end of the appointment period unless otherwise agreed.

Beskrivelse til interne kandidater

The Research Unit of General Practice at the Institute of Public Health, University of Southern Denmark (SDU), invites applications for a 2-year full time Assistant Professor position in Global Health.

The position starts on April 1, 2027, and will terminate at the end of the appointment period unless otherwise agreed.

Job DescriptionThe position involves research in global health with a particular focus on strengthening primary healthcare systems for vulnerable and underserved populations in low- and middle-income countries. The successful candidate will contribute to the international research project STRENGTHENing Gender-Responsive Health Systems for Addressing Non-Communicable Diseases in Climate-Affected Fishing Communities in Western Kenya (STRENGTHEN) and other upcoming global health projects. The STRENGTHEN project aims to improve the prevention and management of NCDs in climate-affected fishing communities in Western Kenya by making the health systems even more gender-responsive. The project will generate evidence on how community health promoters (CHPs) provide NCD care in FEDCs affected by climate change. It will address five key health systems building blocks: health information systems, health workforce, health service, medical technology, and policy and governance. The work will involve conducting implementation and health services research, and collaborating with researchers, healthcare professionals, policymakers, and community stakeholders across different country settings. The position involves travel to Kenya for short periods.

We offer a challenging position in a stimulating research environment with excellent opportunities for collaboration within SDU and with international research partners.

Expectations of qualificationsThe successful applicant should have:

• 
A PhD degree (or equivalent) in Global Health, Public Health, Epidemiology, Health Services Research, Implementation Science, or a related discipline

• 
A strong background in health systems research, primary healthcare, chronic disease prevention and management, or health equity research in low- and middle-income countries

• 
A strong academic record

• 
Good collaboration and communication skills

• 
Interest in co-supervising BSc, MSc and PhD students

Following qualifications are preferred:

• 
Experience with mixed-methods research, including qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis

• 
Experience with implementation science, intervention development, and evaluation of community-based health programmes

• 
Experience with global health research conducted in low- and middle-income countries and/or humanitarian settings

• 
Experience with stakeholder engagement and collaboration with healthcare providers, communities, and policymakers

• 
Experience with writing research applications

• 
Experience in teaching and education

jobs.occupation: A position as postdoc (100% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark. The position is limited to three years.
jobs.description:
A position as postdoc (100% time) is vacant at the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, the Department of Clinical Research, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark. The position is limited to three years. The starting date is 01 February 2027 or later by agreement and depending on the candidate’s preferences.

We are seeking a researcher with documented experience in epidemiological research who can independently plan studies, conduct analyses and write scientific papers. We are looking for a future colleague with a clear academic interest in women’s mental health and the motivation to develop their research in this field. Experience in psychiatric epidemiology is a distinct advantage.

The project

The position is funded by a grant from the Wellcome Trust through PROMIS, an international research project on women’s mental health during perimenopause. The project is in its initial phase and will draw on cohort data linked to national registers, in collaboration with researchers in the UK, the USA and Sweden.

The project investigates risk factors for the onset or recurrence of depression, anxiety, bipolar disorder and psychotic disorders during perimenopause. The work includes epidemiological studies of risk, the development and validation of prediction models, and studies of hormone therapy and mental health outcomes using target trial emulation.

Research tasks

The postdoc will work closely with Principal Investigator Professor Trine Munk-Olsen and the project’s data analyst and participate actively in the international research collaboration. The candidate will have considerable scope to shape research questions, the structure of individual studies, study designs and methodological choices within the framework of the project.

The main tasks are to:

• 
Plan and conduct epidemiological studies using register and cohort data, including preparing study protocols and analysis plans.

• 
Independently perform statistical analyses, interpret results and write scientific papers.

• 
Identify risk factors for mental disorders during perimenopause and contribute to the development and validation of prediction models.

• 
Contribute to studies using target trial emulation to investigate hormone therapy and mental health outcomes.

• 
Together with other project team members, contribute to applications for access to external datasets and to the maintenance, quality assurance, harmonisation and documentation of the datasets used.

• 
Participate in subprojects and undertake tasks within the international collaboration, including coordination, organising project meetings and following up on joint agreements.

The position will involve limited travel. It is primarily research-oriented. Teaching and supervision duties may be included, depending also on the candidate’s interests and preferences.

Expectations of qualifications

The applicant who is hired must have a Ph.D. degree in epidemiology, health sciences, biostatistics or data science with a strong focus on health. Candidates who have not yet completed their Ph.D. may apply if they expect to obtain the degree by the starting date. However, we envisage that, in addition to their Ph.D., the candidate will have at least 1–2 years of research-related experience, for example as a postdoc, research assistant or statistician.

The applicant must have the following qualifications:

• 
A clear academic interest in research on women’s mental health, including the relationships between reproductive life stages and mental disorders.

• 
First authorship of several scientific papers, including documented experience in epidemiological research based on register or cohort data.

• 
Documented experience with advanced epidemiological and statistical methods.

• 
Documented experience and competence in statistical programming, for example in R or Stata.

• 
A documented ability to independently plan studies, prepare study protocols, conduct analyses and write scientific papers.

• 
Good collaboration skills and the ability to take responsibility for tasks and contribute constructively to joint research projects.

• 
The ability to work systematically with data quality, documentation and the maintenance of research data.

• 
Fluency in written and spoken English.

The following would be an advantage but are not requirements:

• 
Experience in psychiatric epidemiology.

• 
Experience in the development or validation of prediction models.

• 
Practical experience with target trial emulation.

• 
Experience in international research collaborations.

• 
Written and spoken Danish, as Danish is the working language of the research unit.

Research environment

The position is based in the Research Unit of Child and Adolescent Psychiatry, a growing, dynamic and collaborative research environment at the Department of Clinical Research, University of Southern Denmark. Our research group brings together expertise in psychiatry, psychology, epidemiology and public health. We offer a friendly, inclusive and interdisciplinary working environment where early-career researchers are supported in developing their academic and professional skills. The unit leads several major research projects focusing on perinatal mental health, child and adolescent psychiatry, and early intervention and prevention.

Research strategy for OUH and the Department of Clinical Research

The joint research strategy for the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital sets the direction for our shared research efforts in the years ahead. Rooted in the vision –We conduct research together to shape the patient care of the future – it focuses in particular on: cross-disciplinary research – with people at the centre; strong research environments – as drivers of development; and the research journey – from idea to impact. Further information on the joint research strategy of the Department of Clinical Research and Odense University Hospital is available here.

Further information 

For further information please contact Professor Trine Munk-Olsen, e-mail: tmun@sdu.dk, phone: +45 24 46 62 97.

Application deadline

November 18, 2026, at 23.59 hrs. (CET).

Interviews

Interviews are expected to take place in early December 2026.

Salary and terms of employment

The applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

The position as Postdoc is placed within salary steps 4–8 of the Danish state salary scale, depending on seniority. In addition, a centrally agreed postdoc allowance is paid, and further qualification- and function-related allowances may be negotiated.

The work location will be at Hospitalsringen 90, 5260 Odense S.  

Application

Applications must be submitted electronically using the link “Apply now” - see below.

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

Only applications written in English will be accepted for evaluation.

The application must include (as PDF files) (please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total):

• 
a motivation letter

• 
a detailed CV

• 
degree certificates (inclusive of Ph.D.-diploma)

• 
a complete and numbered list of publications

3 scientific peer-reviewed publications considered by the candidate as most important for this position. Please note that a copy of each publication must be attached as a pdf file.

a teaching portfolio detailing the candidate’s prior teaching experience, teaching skills, and teaching philosophy

a detailed description of research experience

an explanation of other qualifications relevant to the position

Shortlisting will be used as part of the initial selection process. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material. 

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive part of the evaluation that concerns themselves. 

References will be obtained for the preferred candidate from their current and previous employers. Applicants invited for interview should expect to complete a work-related personality assessment.

Living and working in Denmark

Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. 

The International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. 

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

 Candidate and university outreach.

 Work with our CRM system, HubSpot.

jobs.occupation: Associate Professor in Public Health: Children and Young People
jobs.description:
At the National Institute of Public Health (NIPH), University of Southern Denmark (SDU), a position as Associate Professor in Public Health is hereby advertised with a focus on interdisciplinary, qualitative studies of children’s and young people’s health and well-being, commencing on 15 April 2027 or as soon as possible thereafter.About your future research environment  

The National Institute of Public Health (NIPH) is part of the University of Southern Denmark and is located in Copenhagen. As a national public health institute, we conduct research to improve public health in Denmark and Greenland. At the same time, we contribute internationally to the development of knowledge, theories and methods in the field of public health.

We offer an inspiring research environment in the heart of Copenhagen with skilled and dedicated colleagues from diverse research and educational backgrounds. Here, you will have the opportunity for academic exchange and further development of your own research areas, as well as participation in national and international networks. The position is anchored in the research group Health Promotion and Interventions, which conducts research on interventions addressing public health issues and works with methodological and theoretical challenges related to the design and evaluation of intervention and implementation studies. Our research concerns children, young people and families, as well as vulnerable and disadvantaged groups, and takes place in a range of settings, including daycare institutions, primary and lower secondary schools, upper secondary education, the healthcare system, municipal services, supermarkets and local communities.  You will actively participate in the daily activities of the research group and work closely with other researchers at NIPH.  

The duties include research, teaching and dissemination within the institute’s areas of expertise, including:  - Children’s and young people’s health, well-being and everyday life- The significance of digital media for children’s and young people’s lives and health- Health promotion and implementation research in daycare institutions, schools and upper secondary education- Interdisciplinary, practice-oriented research and development projects, including process evaluation- Advanced qualitative methods, including ethnography, interviews, focus groups and child-centred approaches- Teaching and supervision at bachelor’s and master’s level, including qualitative methods, children’s and young people’s health, and implementation- Preparation of applications for external funding as well as project management and coordination- Contributions to the further development of the research environment, including method development and research group activities The following qualifications are highly valued:  You have established yourself as a qualified researcher within qualitative methods, children’s and young people’s health, and intervention and implementation research, and you possess strong research and teaching qualifications at a high level. You have a relevant publication profile and extensive experience in disseminating research to researchers, practitioners, and other target groups. You have broad collaborative networks and experience in research collaboration with practitioners. As a person, you are dedicated and possess strong communication skills. You are able to build trusting relationships with students, colleagues, and external partners alike. As a teacher, you communicate up-to-date, relevant knowledge in an engaging, clear and understandable way, and as a supervisor you are skilled, inspiring, and supportive.  Qualifications  - A PhD degree in Public Health, Education, Sociology, Anthropology or a related field- Experience with intervention and implementation research- Documented experience in research on children’s and young people’s health- A strong profile within qualitative research- Experience in collaborating with practitioners, exchanging knowledge and disseminating research- Experience in national and international research collaboration- Documented teaching experience at university level and experience supervising students (e.g. bachelor’s or master's students)- Proficiency in Danish and English at a high level, both orally and in writing- Documented experience with scientific publications within relevant research areas

Presentable, polite, and service-minded towards customers and colleagues.

A stable workplace with good, dedicated colleagues.

A professional environment for executing your daily tasks.

Opportunities for personal and professional growth (especially in the coordinator role).

Salary based on qualifications.

jobs.occupation: Assistant Professor in Materials for Power Electronics / Printed Electronics
jobs.description:
The cross-border region Denmark-Germany is a powerhouse in industrial electronics. The Centre for Industrial Electronics (CIE) at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) was established by a strong partnership between industry, academia and regional authorities. CIE is located at the campus of SDU Sønderborg and surrounded by a vibrant industrial environment. CIE is part of the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the Faculty of Engineering.

 

Job description 

We are seeking an innovative and visionary Assistant Professor to join the Centre for Industrial Electronics in Sønderborg. The Centre currently has 40 staff, including full and associate professors, assistant professors, postdoctoral researchers, PhD students, and support staff. Funding has been secured to support to establish new research and test laboratories in key areas of industrial electronics. Our ambition is to deliver excellence in research, innovation, and education.

It is our vision that the Centre for Industrial Electronics at SDU will excel in areas of key relevance for companies in the region of Southern Denmark and beyond. 

Candidates are thus required to have a proven research records at least one of the following fields:

• 
General power electronics and its reliability

• 
Multimaterial additive manufacturing

• 
Printed electronics

• 
Polymer composites and nanocomposites for energy applications

• 
Surface and interface engineering

• 
Dielectric materials and capacitor technology

• 
Materials for power electronics

• 
Energy-device manufacturing

• 
Sustainable and circular electronics

 

Qualifications

The candidates must have a PhD in Electrical Engineering/Materials science/Mechanical engineering, or a closely related discipline. 

We also expect:

• 
An outstanding research and publication track record 

• 
Experience with industrial collaboration

• 
Research experience in multi-material additive manufacturing of functional polymer composites

• 
Experience developing polymer nanocomposite dielectrics and thin-film capacitors

• 
Knowledge of nanoparticle surface modification, dispersion, and interface engineering

• 
Hands-on experience in materials processing, device fabrication, and electrical characterization

• 
Ability to investigate relationships between material structure, manufacturing conditions, and electrical performance

• 
Peer-reviewed publications in functional materials, additive manufacturing, or energy-device research

• 
Experience collaborating across materials science and electrical engineering.

Further desirable qualifications:

• 
Experience with bio-based, self-healing, or temperature-resistant capacitor materials

• 
Knowledge of scalable thin-film fabrication, including layer-by-layer deposition or coating.

• 
Experience translating research into industrial applications, particularly embedded heating, sensing, or battery-conditioning systems.

• 
Experience preparing research proposals, securing research resources, and training students.

 

Contact and further information

For information about the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical engineering, which encompasses SDU Electrical Engineering please see https://www.sdu.dk/en/ime.

For specific information on section and centre, please visit www.sdu.dk/ee and www.sdu.dk/cie. 

You are also welcome to contact the Head of the CIE, Professor Thomas Ebel (ebel@sdu.dk,  +45 93 50 72 05) for further information. 

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

A panel will assess the qualification of the candidate for the described post based on the submitted material. 

The application should include:

• 
Curriculum Vitae.

• 
Motivated application. 

• 
Ideas for research and development activities.

• 
Account of significant contributions to innovation in Electrical Engineering and Industrial Engineering Electronics.

• 
Complete list of publications.

• 
Publications most relevant to the position. 

• 
Summary and documentation of teaching experience, including account of experience in training students and outreach. You may attach a Teaching Portfolio. 

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation). 

• 
References/reference letters may also be included.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included. 

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as an assistant professor is temporary and for an initial 3-year period, and the position is open from start of 2027.

During employment, the assistant professor will complete the Lecturer Training Programme. 

Employment as an assistant professor requires academic qualifications at a minimum of PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for assistant professor as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.

jobs.description:
Do you have experience with technical or project procurement in a larger international company? Would you like to help develop a global supply chain in an international project-driven organization? Then you may be the Purchaser we are looking for.

We are upgrading, servicing, and operating engine- and biomass-based power plants around the world. This creates a continuous need to source goods and services from subcontractors and ensure reliable transport for our customers.

For our Global Supply Chain department, we are looking for an outgoing and internationally minded colleague with commitment, determination, and a positive attitude. The department consists of 20 employees responsible for procurement, warehousing, and transport of goods and services.

BWSC – Ever better energy! 

Join us in our mission of building a world of sustainable energy and make a meaningful impact on the world of power generation and energy conversion.

BWSC is a leading player in the power generation industry, specializing in the service, operations, and maintenance of power plants. We are seeking to always provide Ever Better Energy whether it comes to optimizing a conventional power plant, operating a biomass power plant or constructing new energy facilities. Our commitment to excellence, innovation, and environmental stewardship sets us apart in the industry.

Your responsibilities

• Support Project Procurement Managers with procurement tasks related to the execution of upgrading, service- and maintenance projects for engine and biomass power plants globally.
• Obtain quotations from suppliers and place purchase orders within a defined area of responsibility.
• Participate in broader departmental activities such as category management, supplier relationship development, negotiations, and implementation of supplier agreements.
• Contribute to identifying and evaluating potential suppliers.
• Convert purchase requisitions into purchase orders.
• Maintain and update various data, including supplier data, in the ERP system.
• Follow up on purchase orders, deliveries and invoice approvals.
• Assist with various development-oriented Global Supply Chain tasks within BWSC, including work instructions and new workflows.
The work is carried out in close collaboration with other departments in a dynamic and project-oriented organization. A flexible, cooperative, and positive attitude is therefore essential.

Desired Background and Qualifications

• Experience within procurement, including purchase order placement and follow-up.
• Completed education as an office assistant and/or relevant higher education qualification.
• Minimum 3 years of practical experience with technical or project procurement.
• Strong written and spoken English skills.
• Good IT skills and experience with ERP systems, preferably Microsoft Dynamics 365 Business Central.
• Ability to work in a structured manner and meet deadlines.
What do we offer? 

At BWSC we build inspiring careers locally and internationally and give you access to a great network of possibilities. 

We offer you a position with great colleagues and the opportunity to bring your skills into play and grow professionally and personally. As a Purchaser at BWSC, you will receive a competitive starting salary and a strong reward package.

We offer an exciting position in a skilled, collaborative, and project-driven work environment, with opportunities for professional development and growth.

We have a good canteen, fitness facilities, and an active Staff Club that organizes various events and activities. Our HQ is located in Allerød, close to the train station and only a 30-minute ride from central Copenhagen.

Ready for a challenge?  

We review applications and invite relevant candidates for interviews on an ongoing basis, so please apply as soon as possible.

If you have any questions regarding the position, please contact Supply Chain Manager Anders S. A. Pedersen at asap@bwsc.dk.

BWSC is committed to promoting equality and diversity. We encourage all qualified candidates to apply, regardless of ethnic background, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion, or age. Therefore, we do not recommend specifying age, etc., in the application. 

BWSC no longer receives or handles applications received via email due to GDPR requirements. In order for your application to be processed, you must submit your application via our online recruitment system. 

Get to know us even better on our website, www.bwsc.com, where you can learn more about our business, organization, project portfolio, and what we want to achieve at BWSC. 

About BWSC 

Burmeister & Wain Scandinavian Contractor A/S (BWSC) is a global power plant Operation & Maintenance and technical service provider with engineering expertise, enabling power plant owners to deliver cleaner and affordable energy. We are experts in servicing, upgrading, operating, and maintaining energy systems for diesel, natural gas, and renewable baseload power plants worldwide. We help our customers increase reliability and availability of energy production, improve efficiency and performance of their power plant, design and integrate future-proof technologies, and secure lower cost of maintenance.

Our people are at the core of everything we do and key to building strong relationships with our customers. We invest in our people and their wellbeing, supporting professional development and creating an environment where collaboration, knowledge sharing, and personal growth drive our continued success and growth as a company.

jobs.occupation: Postdoctoral position in computational modeling of visual perception
jobs.description:
The Department of Psychology, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a fully funded postdoctoral position in computational modeling of visual perception. The position is available for up to 36 months and is part of a project led by Dr. Gregory Scott Francis that is supported by the SDU Department of Psychology. The starting date is March 15, 2026, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Research environment

The postdoc will be affiliated with the Research Unit of Health and Cognitive Psychology. The position is at the SDU Esbjerg campus but will also involve interaction with staff at the SDU Odense campus. 

Project description

A basic process of the visual system is to monitor the location and characteristics of objects in a scene, and the multiple object tracking (MOT) paradigm has identified many fundamental aspects of this process. With a rich literature of empirical results, this paradigm is ready for theoretical development, which this project intends to pursue using an integrate-and-fire neural network model known as LAMINART. A key aspect of the model is the ability to select/segment visual objects, which may explain how people can (seemingly) effortlessly track multiple objects in a dynamic visual scene. 

The successful candidate will be required to design, program and analyze an integrate-and-fire neural network model of visual perception. Good programming (Python) skills are required along with a good understanding of empirical methods and ways to connect empirical findings with model behavior. The position also involves teaching duties.

The project involves collaboration with Prof. Søren Krogh Andersen, also at SDU.

Qualifications

Ideally, applicants for the position should satisfy the following requirements:

• 
PhD level in psychology, cognitive (neuro)science, vision science, or a related field

• 
Research experience as evidenced by conference contributions and peer-reviewed journal articles in a field related to the offered position

• 
Expertise in visual attention and perception

• 
Strong analytical skills, including the ability to design, implement, and analyze complex experiments

• 
Be willing and able to teach for the Department of Psychology

• 
Prior experience with neural network modeling is a plus

• 
Prior experience with cognitive modelling is a plus

• 
Good command of statistics

• 
Good command of Python (or similar programming languages and a willingness to learn)

• 
Very good command of the English language in spoken and written form

• 
Some knowledge of the Danish language is a plus

Candidates who are about to obtain these qualifications are also encouraged to apply. 

Contact information

For further information about the position, please contact Dr. Greg Francis, SDU (email: gfrancis@health.sdu.dk; phone: +45 65 50 16 98), or Professor Søren Krogh Andersen (email: skandersen@health.sdu.dk; phone: +45 65 50 49 57)

Application deadline

The application deadline is November 08, 2026, at 23.59 hrs. CET.

Salary and terms of employment

The base salary for a postdoctoral researcher is DKK 36,877.42, with an additional job structure supplement of DKK 5,230.75. This brings the total monthly salary to DKK 42,108.16.

The successful applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations).

Application

Applications must be in English and submitted electronically using the link "Apply now". 

Attached files must be in Adobe PDF format.

We strongly recommend that you read How to apply for a position at SDU before you apply.

The application must include (as PDF files) (please note that the application (the motivation letter) and CV must not exceed 10 MB in total):

• 
A letter of motivation (max. 1 page)

• 
A detailed CV

• 
Master and PhD degree certificates, if available

• 
A complete and numbered list of publications 

• 
Three scientific publications (or preprints) considered to be most important for the advertised position (please note that one file per publication must be submitted)

• 
Contact details of at least two university supervisors or employers who can provide references

If you experience technical problems, you must contact hcm-support@sdu.dk.

Please note that all the above-mentioned information must be included in the application. 

Incomplete applications and applications received after the application deadline will not be considered. 

Shortlisting of applications may be used in the initial selection process.

Living and working in Denmark

Foreign applicants will be offered Danish language training as part of the employment. 

The International Staff Office (ISO) at SDU provides a variety of services for new employees, guests and people who consider applying for a job at the University of Southern Denmark. 

The University wishes our staff to reflect the diversity of society and thus welcomes applications from all qualified candidates regardless of personal background.

jobs.occupation: PhD Position in Data-driven Critical Raw Material Supply Chain Resilience
jobs.description:
Do you want to investigate the resilience of critical raw material supply chains supporting low-carbon and digital technologies? Join us as a PhD student at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, University of Southern Denmark.

The Department of Green Technology at the University of Southern Denmark invites applications for a three-year PhD position in data-driven critical raw material supply chain resilience.

The position will be based at SDU Life Cycle Engineering, Department of Green Technology, Faculty of Engineering, at the SDU Odense campus. The expected starting date is 15 February 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

 

Project Overview

The deployment of low-carbon technologies, electrification and digital infrastructure is increasing global demand for critical raw materials. At the same time, the production and processing of many of these materials are geographically concentrated and exposed to geopolitical, economic, environmental and logistical disruptions.

Understanding how technology development affects material demand, in-use stocks, end-of-life flows and global supply dependencies is therefore important for assessing and strengthening the resilience of critical raw material supply chains.

The PhD position is jointly funded through research projects on critical raw material supply chains and material requirements for Denmark’s climate-neutral transition. The project will be embedded in an interdisciplinary research environment combining environmental systems analysis, supply-chain research and data science.

 

PhD Topic Description

The PhD project will develop modular and data-driven approaches for analysing critical raw material demand, supply-chain dependencies and resilience.

A central methodological contribution will be the development of transparent, reusable and reproducible computational modules for dynamic material flow analysis. The modules will support the integration of technology deployment scenarios, material intensities, product lifetimes, stocks and flows, end-of-life management, recycling, production, trade, facility and ownership data.

The developed approaches will be applied to selected technology systems, including Denmark’s wind-energy infrastructure and the rapidly expanding infrastructure supporting data centres and AI computing. These cases will be analysed within a common methodological framework to examine how infrastructure expansion and technological change influence demand for critical and scarce materials, in-use stocks, future waste flows, recycling potential and global supply-chain dependencies.

The project may also investigate overlapping material requirements and competition for materials across low-carbon and digital technologies. Particular attention may be given to supply concentration, host–by-product dependencies, trade and ownership structures, supply bottlenecks, cascading risks and potential resilience strategies.

Depending on the candidate’s academic background and the specific research questions, the project may include network analysis, geospatial analysis, scenario modelling, uncertainty analysis, machine learning and other AI-supported approaches.

The candidate will build on selected existing models, datasets and research activities in the group and further develop scientifically robust and reusable methods that improve transparency, comparability and reproducibility in material-system research.

The exact research focus and detailed PhD plan will be developed jointly with the successful candidate, taking into account the project objectives, academic background and research interests.

In addition to a PhD dissertation and high-quality scientific publications, the project is expected to produce reusable modelling methods, documented datasets and reproducible computational workflows.

 

PhD Position and Research Environment

As a PhD student, you will conduct independent research under the supervision of an interdisciplinary team, contribute to high-quality scientific publications and participate actively in a collaborative research environment.

You will join SDU Life Cycle Engineering, where research covers industrial ecology, material flow analysis, life cycle assessment, circular economy, resource systems and sustainability transitions.

The project connects expertise in engineering, data science, mathematics, business, supply-chain research and geological resources. The wider research environment includes competences in material flow analysis, critical raw material systems, data mining, network analysis, supply-chain science, finance, investment, ownership structures, geological resources and technology systems.

The position provides opportunities for collaboration across SDU faculties and with external research partners. It may also include participation in international conferences, research visits and collaboration with relevant industrial and public-sector stakeholders.

The PhD programme follows the Danish PhD framework and includes coursework, participation in active research environments, dissemination activities, and teaching or other knowledge-dissemination duties.

 

What We Expect

We are looking for a highly motivated, independent and collaborative candidate with a strong interest in critical raw materials, quantitative modelling, data-driven research and sustainability.

Applicants must hold a relevant master’s degree or equivalent by the time of enrolment. Relevant academic backgrounds may include engineering, industrial ecology, sustainability science, resource management, data science, computer science, applied mathematics, operations research, supply-chain management, geoinformatics, mining or geological sciences, or another relevant natural science or quantitative discipline.

The successful candidate should demonstrate:

• 
A solid academic foundation in quantitative analysis, system modelling, data science or related methods. 

• 
Experience with programming and data analysis, preferably using Python or a similar programming language. 

• 
Experience with data handling, including data cleaning, transformation, integration and exploratory analysis. 

• 
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills. 

• 
The ability to work independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary research environment. 

• 
Good written and spoken English. 

• 
A strong interest in sustainability, critical raw materials and supply-chain resilience. 

Experience in one or more of the following areas will be considered an advantage:

• 
Material flow analysis, industrial ecology or material systems modelling. 

• 
Network, supply-chain or geospatial analysis. 

• 
Scientific computing and reproducible research workflows. 

• 
Statistics, machine learning, artificial intelligence, optimisation, uncertainty or scenario analysis. 

• 
International trade, production facility or corporate ownership data. 

• 
Critical raw materials, wind energy, digital infrastructure or data centres. 

Applicants are not expected to possess expertise in all these areas. Prior experience with material flow analysis is an advantage but is not a requirement. Relevant training will be provided according to the candidate’s background and the needs of the project.

 

Application

Before applying the candidates are advised to read the Faculty information for prospective PhD students and the SDU information on how to apply.

The application must be submitted in English through the SDU online recruitment system.

Assessment of applicants will be based on the submitted application material. The application must include:

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
A motivated application describing the applicant’s research interests, relevant qualifications and motivation for applying. 

• 
Documentation of academic qualifications, including bachelor’s and master’s degree certificates and complete transcripts of grades. 

• 
Official English translations of documents not issued in English or Danish. 

• 
Two letters of recommendation. 

• 
A list of publications and up to two examples of relevant publications, if available. 

• 
The completed TEK PhD application form for 5+3 applicants. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
The completed TEK form for calculation of grade-point average. Find the form at the Faculty website.

• 
Official documentation describing the grading system of the awarding university, if the degree was not obtained in Denmark. 

• 
Examples of relevant thesis work, software, code repositories or other research outputs, where available. 

• 
Only for applicants from programmes that evaluate thesis/examination project by approved/not approved: An official written assessment of the thesis or dissertation project from the grade giving institution. The statement must clearly state that the candidate has been among the top 30 pct. in the graduation class for the study programme.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

For administrative questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact our email support.

 

The application deadline is November 15, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Enrollment and employment terms

Appointment as a PhD fellow is a 3-year salaried position, and the monthly gross salary incl. pension is 37.075 DKK. If you have relevant postgraduate experience, you may be placed on a higher salary step. The place of employment is in Odense, Denmark and preferred starting date is February 15, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter.

Applicants must hold a master’s degree (equivalent to a Danish master's degree) at the time of enrollment and employment. Employment is contingent on enrollment approved by the PhD School. Enrollment will be in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order). Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for PhD fellows as described therein as well as the Protocol on PhD fellows signed by the Danish Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

-

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

 

SDU Life Cycle Engineering

The successful candidate will be affiliated with SDU Life Cycle Engineering at the Department of Green Technology. The research environment conducts interdisciplinary research on the global and systemic interactions between materials, technologies, energy, the environment and society.

The Department of Green Technology is located in Odense, the main campus of the University of Southern Denmark. Odense offers an international research environment and an open Scandinavian working culture.

 

Further Information

Further information about the scientific content of the position is available from:

Wu ChenAssociate ProfessorDepartment of Green TechnologySDU Life Cycle EngineeringUniversity of Southern DenmarkEmail: wuc@igt.sdu.dk

For administrative questions regarding the recruitment process, please contact our email support.

jobs.occupation: Senior Developer to support the Green Energy Transition
jobs.description:
Are you an experienced software developer with a passion for building high-quality applications? Do you enjoy solving complex technical challenges and working closely with business experts to create solutions that support the efficient, reliable, and secure operation of the Nordic power grid? If you are looking to make an impact in supporting the green transition of the energy sector across Finland, Norway, Sweden and Denmark, you might be the person we are looking for.  

Join a fast-developing Nordic company and become a part of an agile environment where we develop innovative solutions. Nordic RCC is an important contributor to the green energy transition, supporting the Nordic transmission system operators in ensuring efficient and secure operations of the Nordic electricity power system.  

As part of our continued growth, Application Development is expanding significantly. We are strengthening our department with five Senior Developers and two Lead Developers, creating exciting opportunities to join a growing team and help shape the future of software development at Nordic RCC. 

Your role   

As a Senior Developer in Application Development, you will join a collaborative team of approximately 23 developers. Together, you will design, develop, and maintain internal applications that support our current and future business services. Working closely with product owners, architects, engineers, operators, and UX specialists, you will help translate business needs into robust technical solutions. 

You will be part of an application team that values sustainable solutions over quick fixes. We actively collaborate across applications and business services to identify common solutions, increase quality, and continuously improve the way we work. 

What you will do:

• 
Design, develop, and maintain robust applications using C# and .NET. 

• 
Write clean, maintainable, testable, and well-documented code following established design patterns and development standards. 

• 
Transform complex engineering and operational requirements into effective software solutions by collaborating closely with architects, product owners, engineers, operators, and UX designers to build solutions that meet business and operational needs. 

• 
Contribute to technical improvements, modernization efforts, and continuous optimization of existing applications. 

• 
Participate in code reviews and help ensure high quality, reliability, and maintainability across solutions. 

• 
Support troubleshooting and resolution of production issues. 

• 
Serve as a technical role model within the team and mentor colleagues who are developing their technical skills. 

• 
Stay current with new technologies, tools, and development practices relevant to Nordic RCC's technology landscape. 

Technology Stack:

• 
Primary languages and frameworks  C#, .NET, SolidJS, JavaScript/TypeScript, Functional programming, Python  

• 
Architecture, design patterns & integrations  Clean Architecture, SOLID, Event-driven Architecture, Message-driven Architecture, REST APIs 

• 
Databases & Storage Relational databases (SQL Server), NoSQL databases (MongoDB), GridFS, S3 

• 
Infrastructure & Platform (on-prem)  Kubernetes (on-prem), Docker, Rancher, Prometheus/Grafana, ArgoCD, NginX  

• 
Tooling and collaboration  Git, Visual Studio, VS Code, JetBrains Rider, Azure DevOps, CI/CD pipelines 

We’re looking for someone with:  

• 
Collaborative Mindset: You work closely with Application Architects, Product Owners, and fellow developers, contributing technical expertise, mentoring colleagues, and helping to ensure maintainable, scalable, and robust solutions. 

• 
Technical Foundation: A degree in Computer Science, IT, Software Engineering, or a related field. 

• 
Relevant Expertise: Experience developing enterprise-grade applications in C#/.NET, with a solid understanding of software architecture, design patterns, and modern development practices. 

• 
Continuous Improvement: You identify opportunities to improve code quality, system reliability, team practices, and developer productivity. 

• 
Nice to have: Experience working with functional programming, Clean Architecture principles, Azure DevOps, Kubernetes and Scrum processes.  

• 
Energy Sector Knowledge: Familiarity with the power systems domain is a plus but not required.  

 If you do not tick all the boxes, but think you could be a good match, don’t hesitate to apply for this position.   

What We Offer: A Flexible and Inclusive Workplace  

You will join a diverse organization of 23 nationalities, where inclusivity is celebrated, with more than 30% women on board (and a commitment to improving this balance). We are located in Copenhagen Towers office in Ørestad, with the flexibility to balance on-site and remote work 2 days a week.  

At Nordic RCC, we live by the values of fellowship, curiosity, respect, and transparency—values defined by our employees that shape how we collaborate and innovate. If you see yourself thriving in such an environment, we’d love to hear from you.  

Note that as part of the recruitment process, the candidate must undergo a satisfactory background check. The position is also conditioned upon a national security clearance. Both will be facilitated by Nordic RCC. You can read more on security clearance here. Please also note that the process includes that any spouse, registered partner, cohabitant, steady partner, co-resident, child over 18 living at home and parent with the same address as the candidate must also consent to be examined.   

Application deadline and contact information  

Please apply online (in English) no later than 15/11-2026. Interviews will be held on a rolling basis up until the right candidate has been found.  

To ensure a fair and unbiased recruitment process, we kindly request that you do not include photographs in your CVs or application materials.  

A cover letter is not required, but we kindly ask you to include a few sentences in your CV explaining why you are interested in the position. Applications are only accepted through our online recruitment system. 

If you have any questions, please contact Pernille Yde Juul Hansen, Manager, Application Development pyh@nordic-rcc.net / +45 3092 3111

jobs.occupation: Two-year Postdoc position on Spintronic Quantum-inspired Computing
jobs.description:
Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU) invites applications for a 2-year Postdoctoral Researcher position within the newly funded QUANTRONIC – Spintronic Pseudo-Qubits for Room-Temperature Quantum Computing project, supported by the Villum Experiment programme of Villum Fonden.

We are seeking a highly motivated postdoctoral researcher to investigate a new class of spintronic pseudo-qubits (p-qubits) based on spin-orbit torque magnetic tunnel junctions (SOT-MTJs). The project explores whether engineered stochastic spintronic devices can reproduce key computational mechanisms associated with quantum systems - including superposition-like states, probability-amplitude-based interference, and entanglement-like correlations—without relying on fragile quantum coherence or cryogenic operation.

QUANTRONIC is a high-risk, high-gain research project positioned at the intersection of spintronics, probabilistic computing, quantum-inspired computing, nanoelectronics, and integrated circuit design. The central concept is a novel SOT-MTJ architecture designed to represent and manipulate probability amplitudes and to enable synchronization between multiple pseudo-qubits. The project will combine physics-based modelling, device design and fabrication, experimental characterization, and system-level demonstrations.

The successful candidate will work within SDU Microelectronics and collaborate closely with international partners, particularly INL – International Iberian Nanotechnology Laboratory, on the design and fabrication of spintronic devices.

The position is expected to start in February 2027, with the specific starting date to be agreed with the successful candidate.

 

As a Postdoctoral Researcher in QUANTRONIC, your key responsibilities will include:

• 
Develop and refine physics-based compact models of SOT-MTJ-based pseudo-qubits, including stochastic switching and inter-device coupling.

• 
Develop Verilog-A models and integrate them into circuit-level simulation environments such as Cadence.

• 
Investigate the physical requirements for controlling probabilistic states and representing probability amplitudes in spintronic devices.

• 
Collaborate with project partners on the design and fabrication of SOT-MTJ devices and arrays.

• 
Experimentally characterize standalone devices and coupled arrays, including stochastic switching, synchronization, and entanglement-like correlations.

• 
Investigate quantum-inspired gate operations and system-level demonstrations using networks of pseudo-qubits.

• 
Contribute to proof-of-concept demonstrations, including integer factorization and other quantum-inspired computational problems.

• 
Publish research results in high-quality international journals and conferences and contribute to the dissemination of project results.

• 
Collaborate with researchers in spintronics, probabilistic computing, microelectronics, materials science, and quantum information.

 

What we offer

• 
A unique opportunity to work on a high-risk, high-gain research concept exploring a new computational regime between classical probabilistic and quantum computing.

• 
A stimulating research environment within SDU Microelectronics, a growing research section with expertise in spintronics, probabilistic computing, neuromorphic computing, analog/digital IC design, and emerging computing architectures.

• 
Access to advanced facilities for electronic design, device characterization, measurement, and system prototyping.

• 
Close collaboration with INL – International Iberian Nanotechnology Laboratory on spintronic device technology and fabrication.

• 
Opportunities to collaborate with national and international researchers in spintronics, quantum-inspired computing, quantum technologies, and nanoelectronics.

• 
An open, international, and collaborative research environment within SDU's Faculty of Engineering, supporting interdisciplinary research across electronics, physics, materials science, and computing.

• 
Strong opportunities for developing an independent research profile in an emerging area of probabilistic and quantum-inspired hardware.

 

What we expect

Applicants should hold a PhD in electronic engineering, electrical engineering, applied physics, nanotechnology, spintronics, or a closely related field.

The ideal candidate should have experience in one or more of the following areas:

• 
Spintronics and magnetic devices, particularly MTJs, STT-MTJs, SOT-MTJs, or related technologies.

• 
Physics-based modelling of nanoscale or magnetic devices.

• 
Verilog-A, SPICE, and Cadence or comparable circuit/device simulation environments.

• 
Experimental characterization of electronic, magnetic, or spintronic devices.

• 
Stochastic or probabilistic computing systems.

Experience in micromagnetic simulation, magnetotransport measurements, nanofabrication, probabilistic computing, or quantum/quantum-inspired computing will be considered a strong advantage.

We are particularly interested in candidates who are enthusiastic about working across traditional disciplinary boundaries and are comfortable combining device physics, modelling, experimentation, and computing concepts.

The successful candidate should be able to work independently while contributing actively to an interdisciplinary and international research team. Excellent written and spoken English and strong communication skills are required.

 

Workplace description 

The successful candidate will join SDU Microelectronics, a dynamic and expanding section at the Institute of Mechanical and Electrical Engineering (IME). The section conducts internationally recognized research in integrated circuits, spintronics, photonics, and neuromorphic computing, and plays a central role in SDU’s ambition to be a national and European hub for semiconductor and chip innovation. 

 

Further information 

For further information about the position, please contact Professor Farshad Moradi (moradi@sdu.dk / email), Head of the SDU Microelectronics section and Associate Professor Hooman Farkhani (farkhani@sdu.dk / email), Deputy Head of SDU Microelectronics. 

If you experience technical problems, please contact our email support.

 

Application

Applicants are advised to read the SDU information on how to apply.

Assessment of the candidates is based on the application material, and the application must include: 

• 
Motivated application.

• 
Curriculum Vitae. 

• 
Master’s and PhD degree certificates or equivalent (original and an official English translation).  

• 
Complete list of publications.

• 
Publications most relevant to the position.

• 
Summary and documentation of experience in teaching, if relevant to the position. 

• 
A research statement may be included.

• 
References/reference letters may also be included.

• 
A statement/documentation of other qualifications relevant to the position may also be included.

All documents must be in English and PDF format. CPR number (civil registration number) must be crossed out. All PDF-files must be unlocked, allow binding and may not be password protected. 

SUBMISSION GUIDE: Motivated application must be uploaded under ‘Cover letter’ (max. 5 MB), Curriculum Vitae must be uploaded under ‘Resume’ (max 5 MB). All other documents must be uploaded under ‘Miscellaneous documents’ (max 10 files with a maximum 50 MB per file). 

 

The application deadline is November 10, 2026, at 11:59 PM/23:59 (CET/CEST) 

 

Assessment and selection process

Applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. Shortlisting may be applied, and only shortlisted candidates will receive a written assessment. Read about shortlisting at SDU.  Interviews and tests may be part of the overall evaluation. Read about the Assessment and selection process.  

 

Employment terms

Appointment as a postdoc is temporary for an initial 2-year period, and the preferred start date is February 2027. Extension may be possible depending on available funding.

Employment as a postdoc requires academic qualifications at PhD level at the time of employment. Employment will be in accordance with the collective agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations for academics in the state including the associated circular on the protocol for the job structure for academic staff at Danish universities and the provisions for postdoc as described therein. 

Salary is determined in accordance with the applicable collective agreement and based on objective and gender-neutral criteria, including the content of the position, responsibilities, and qualification requirements. As an applicant, you are entitled to information about the starting salary and salary range for the position. This information will be provided during the recruitment process. SDU does not collect information on applicants’ previous salary. Further information on salary and taxation. 

Persons employed in the position may, based on a specific individual managerial assessment, be exempted from time registration, also known as a “self-organizer”.

 

The University of Southern Denmark wishes its staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, is subject to a number of security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position(s).

Further information for international applicants about entering and working in Denmark. You may also visit WorkinDenmark for additional information.

Further information about The Faculty of Engineering.
